cases.learnTitle: Encapsulated papillary carcinoma with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) on breast ultrasound (biopsy-proven; radiologist outline)
cases.contextSource: Age and clinical signs from the dataset's clinical data.
cases.referenceSummary: The lesion is outlined freehand by a radiologist experienced in breast ultrasound, who also recorded its BI-RADS descriptors (Breast-Lesions-USG): shape oval, margin circumscribed, echo pattern complex cystic/solid, posterior features enhancement, BI-RADS 4b. Biopsy: encapsulated papillary carcinoma with ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) (malignant). The image is the dataset's cropped B-mode frame with its true pixel size; no Doppler, no orientation.
cases.learnNotes: Breast ultrasound first answers one question: cyst or solid? A simple cyst is anechoic (black, no internal echoes), circumscribed with a thin sharp back wall, and has posterior acoustic enhancement (brighter tissue behind it, because fluid lets the sound through). Anything that fails these criteria is treated as solid or complicated. A solid mass is described like a mammographic one: shape (oval, round, irregular), orientation, margin (circumscribed or not: indistinct, angular, microlobulated, spiculated), echo pattern and posterior features. An oval, circumscribed mass parallel to the skin favors a benign tumor such as a fibroadenoma; an irregular, spiculated or angular hypoechoic mass with posterior shadowing is suspicious for carcinoma. Ultrasound shows the features; the biopsy gives the diagnosis.

cases.referenceSummary: The lesion is outlined freehand by a radiologist experienced in breast ultrasound, who also recorded its BI-RADS descriptors (Breast-Lesions-USG): shape oval, margin circumscribed, echo pattern anechoic, posterior features enhancement, BI-RADS 2. Benign: confirmed on follow-up, without biopsy (the radiologist's impression: seroma). The image is the dataset's cropped B-mode frame with its true pixel size; no Doppler, no orientation.
cases.learnNotes: Breast ultrasound first answers one question: cyst or solid? A simple cyst is anechoic (black, no internal echoes), circumscribed with a thin sharp back wall, and has posterior acoustic enhancement (brighter tissue behind it, because fluid lets the sound through). Anything that fails these criteria is treated as solid or complicated. A solid mass is described like a mammographic one: shape (oval, round, irregular), orientation, margin (circumscribed or not: indistinct, angular, microlobulated, spiculated), echo pattern and posterior features. An oval, circumscribed mass parallel to the skin favors a benign tumor such as a fibroadenoma; an irregular, spiculated or angular hypoechoic mass with posterior shadowing is suspicious for carcinoma. Ultrasound shows the features; the biopsy gives the diagnosis.

tasks.explanation: Breast ultrasound first answers one question: cyst or solid? A simple cyst is anechoic (black, no internal echoes), circumscribed with a thin sharp back wall, and has posterior acoustic enhancement (brighter tissue behind it, because fluid lets the sound through). Anything that fails these criteria is treated as solid or complicated. A solid mass is described like a mammographic one: shape (oval, round, irregular), orientation, margin (circumscribed or not: indistinct, angular, microlobulated, spiculated), echo pattern and posterior features. An oval, circumscribed mass parallel to the skin favors a benign tumor such as a fibroadenoma; an irregular, spiculated or angular hypoechoic mass with posterior shadowing is suspicious for carcinoma. Ultrasound shows the features; the biopsy gives the diagnosis. The image carries its pixel size, so the tolerance is a true 3 mm.
